Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Sliding-window rate limiter blocks rapid replay; DFA enforces IDLE→RATE_CHECK before any replay attempt.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: Replayed video/photo blocked by PAD; physical credential replay (NFC cloning) not covered.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Session tokens are 60s TTL, one-time-use (used flag in DB); NFC UID required fresh per session.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Encrypted embeddings prevent offline replay; bearer token replay still possible within TTL.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Hash chain detects duplicate vote records; does not prevent token replay before recording.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: PQC does not directly mitigate replay; session layer handles it.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Limits spoof attempt rate; determined attacker can retry after cooldown.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: MiniFASNetV2 detects printed photo and video replay attacks; APCER_print=5%, APCER_replay=10%.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Requires valid NFC card in addition to face; reduces but does not eliminate spoofing risk.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Encryption at rest does not defend against live spoofing.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Integrity layer does not defend against input spoofing.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Signature layer does not defend against biometric spoofing.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter does not address network-layer MITM.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD is local; does not address MITM on session transport.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Local biometric decision reduces reliance on network auth; session token still transmittable.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: AES-256-GCM with authenticated encryption; session token sent over TLS (assumed channel).

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Hash-chained votes detect tampering post-record; MITM during submission window is not covered.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Dilithium-3 vote signatures prevent forged or altered votes in transit; quantum-resistant.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: DFA stage 1: 5 failures per 300 s per NFC UID; attacker blocked before reaching biometric stage.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD prevents rapid face-image cycling; latency overhead also limits throughput.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Requires physical NFC card; brute-force on face alone is rejected without card.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Argon2id (64 MB, t=3) makes offline brute-force on stolen encrypted embeddings infeasible.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Brute-force at auth stage; vote integrity layer not relevant here.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: PQC does not address online brute-force on biometric system.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter slows repeated attempts but does not prevent a second auth for a different NFC clone.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD verifies liveness but not has_voted status.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: DFA ELIGIBILITY_CHECK: has_voted=True → REJECTED before face stage. Formally proved (property 5).

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Encryption does not address double-vote logic.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Append-only hash chain with unique vote_id; duplicate submission breaks chain integrity.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Signed vote_id prevents silent substitution; chain-level uniqueness is primary defence.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter + one-voter-one-ballot enforced by DFA eligibility stage.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD prevents dummy face images; requires physical voter presence.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Each NFC card is unique; registered voter set is closed at enrollment.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Encryption does not address ballot stuffing.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: External verifier can audit Merkle root against registered voter count; stuffed votes break consistency.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Signed ballots traceable; stuffed unsigned ballots would fail signature verification.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter does not address coercion.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: Physical presence at camera makes remote coercion harder; does not prevent in-person coercion.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Face biometric confirms voter identity; does not prevent coerced compliance.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Vote integrity does not address coercion.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: PQC does not address coercion. (Future: deniable voting / panic PIN.)

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter applies equally to insiders; privileged access still possible.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: Insider with DB access can bypass PAD.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Biometric binding reduces insider ability to vote as another person without physical card+face.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Encrypted embeddings + Argon2id: insider cannot extract plaintext templates without voter PIN/key.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Immutable append-only audit log; insider modifications break hash chain and are detectable.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Vote signatures non-repudiable; insider cannot forge signed votes without signing key.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Per-UID sliding window prevents single-UID exhaustion; PAD latency limits throughput of DoS via face.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD adds 15 ms overhead; limits face-submission DoS rate.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Fusion computation is lightweight; does not defend against network-level DoS.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Crypto layer does not address DoS.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Integrity layer does not address DoS.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter is not cryptographic; not relevant to quantum threat.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Biometric fusion not cryptographic; quantum adversary could break classical session KEM.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: AES-256-GCM is quantum-resistant (Grover's requires 2^128 work); Argon2id key derivation unaffected.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: SHA-256 is quantum-resistant (128-bit post-quantum security); Merkle proofs remain secure.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Dilithium-3 (NIST FIPS 204, ML-DSA-65) and Kyber-768 (FIPS 203, ML-KEM-768) are quantum-resistant.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter does not prevent physical access.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: Stolen device still requires live face at camera; printed photo attempts blocked by PAD.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Stolen device without voter's NFC card and live face cannot authenticate.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: All data at rest encrypted; stolen SD card yields only ciphertext without voter-derived key.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Past votes are immutably recorded; stolen device does not allow retroactive modification.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Signing keys stored encrypted; physical access without key derivation does not yield signing capability.

Rate limiter\n(DFA stage 1).rationale: Rate limiter logs events but does not protect the audit store.

PAD liveness\n(Stage 5).rationale: PAD does not protect audit store.

Bayesian\nfusion (NFC+face).rationale: Fusion does not protect audit store.

AES-256-GCM\n+ Argon2id.rationale: Audit events in SQLite; encryption of DB at OS level partial defence; no HMAC on audit rows.

Hash-chain\n+ Merkle proof.rationale: Vote records hash-chained; any modification breaks chain. External Merkle root can be published for verification.

PQC signatures\n(Dilithium-3).rationale: Dilithium-3 signatures on vote records; forged entries lack valid signature and break chain.
